Two Sum: return the indices of two numbers that add up to target

For each number, check whether target - num is already in a map of value → index. One pass.
Time O(n) · Space O(n). Brute force is O(n²) with two loops.
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (one transaction)

Track the minimum price seen so far, and the best profit from selling today.
O(n) / O(1)
Maximum Subarray Sum (Kadane's algorithm)

At each element, either extend the current subarray or start a new one there: cur = max(x, cur + x).
O(n) / O(1). It also works when every number is negative.
Move Zeroes to the end (keep the order of the others)
Rotate Array right by k steps

Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k, then reverse the rest.
O(n) / O(1)
Product of Array Except Self (no division)

The answer at i is (product of everything to its left) × (product of everything to its right). Do one pass for each.
O(n) / O(1) extra (not counting the output array)
Find the Missing Number in 0..n
O(n) / O(1). XOR works because a ^ a = 0.
Find the Duplicate Number (array of n+1 values in 1..n)
Treat each value as a pointer to the next index. A duplicate creates a cycle, so use Floyd's cycle detection. This doesn't modify the array and uses O(1) space.
Majority Element (appears more than n/2 times)

Boyer-Moore voting: keep a candidate and a count. A match increments the count, a mismatch decrements it, and at zero you switch to the current element.
O(n) / O(1)
Contains Duplicate / find all duplicates in an array
O(n) / O(n)
Merge Intervals

Sort by start time. If the next interval overlaps the last merged one, extend that one's end. Otherwise start a new interval.
O(n log n) / O(n)
Subarray Sum Equals K (handles negatives)

Prefix sums. If prefix[j] - prefix[i] = k, the subarray between them sums to k. Keep a count of each prefix sum seen so far.
O(n) / O(n)
Longest Consecutive Sequence (unsorted, in O(n))
Put everything in a HashSet. Only start counting from numbers where x-1 isn't in the set, i.e. the start of a sequence.
Sort Colors / Dutch National Flag (0s, 1s and 2s)
One pass, O(n) / O(1)
Merge Two Sorted Arrays (into the first one, which has spare space)
Top K Frequent Elements

Count frequencies with a map, then keep a min-heap of size k ordered by frequency. Bucket sort gives O(n).
O(n log k) / O(n)
Spiral Matrix: return all elements in spiral order
Shrink four boundaries after each side. The two if checks stop a single remaining row or column from being added twice. O(R·C) time, O(1) extra space.
Set Matrix Zeroes (in place, O(1) extra space)

Use the first row and first column as marker arrays, with one extra flag for column 0 (because m[0][0] can only mark one of them). The simple version uses two boolean arrays for O(R + C) space. O(R·C) time.
Next Permutation

The suffix after the dip is non-increasing, so swapping in the next larger value and reversing the suffix gives the smallest larger arrangement. If there is no dip, the array is the last permutation and the reverse wraps it to the first. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Maximum Product Subarray

Kadane's variant: track both the largest and the smallest product ending here, because a very negative product becomes the largest after multiplying by a negative. A zero resets both. O(n) time, O(1) space.
First Missing Positive (O(n) time, O(1) space)

The answer is always in 1..n+1, so the array itself can act as the hash set ("index as hash" / cyclic sort). Each swap puts one value in its final slot, so the total work is O(n) despite the inner loop. The same trick solves "find all duplicates" and "find all disappeared numbers".
Range Sum Query with prefix sums (1D and 2D)

O(n) (or O(R·C)) preprocessing, then every query is O(1). The extra leading 0 row/column removes edge cases. If values are updated frequently, a Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree) gives O(log n) for both update and query.
